course_title: Creating classrooms of the future with digital technologies across learning areas
course_description:
This course explores the barriers and enablers around integrating educational technologies into classroom practices both now and into the future. It offers you an opportunity to engage with contemporary research, theories, technologies and practice-based models in order to develop and refine your own pedagogical vision and approaches to technology-enhanced teaching and learning practices.

This course may not be offered in person if the enrolment is less than 10 students.

The uptake and integration of educational technology for teaching and learning is a developing issue across all educational sectors and, thus, a crucial area of study and research. Various enablers and barriers contribute to this issue and require closer examination. As educators, it is important to reflect carefully on the interrelationships between our beliefs and pedagogy and the technology affordances available for our classroom practices in the physical and virtual learning spaces available.

In order to create classrooms of the future with educational technology, we need to develop coherent pedagogical visions for how student learning can be enriched as well as strong understandings of the theories and instructional design elements that underpin effective technology practices and integration.

Note that this course does not include software training however students are encouraged to explore and use technologies of interest.

course_aims: This course explores the barriers and enablers around integrating educational technologies into classroom practices both now and into the future. It offers you an opportunity to engage with contemporary research, theories, technologies and practice-based models in order to develop and refine your own pedagogical vision and approaches to technology practice. You will explore issues around the uptake and integration of technology in classrooms and the role of pedagogical beliefs and vision. You will evaluate your own conceptual understandings and draw on scholarly research and learning and instructional design theories. This course will challenge you with contentious issues and require you to evaluate good practice models in order to characterise elements of enriching technology-enhanced educational practices that are meaningful for your professional context.

learning_outcomes.description: Review and reflect on the common enablers and barriers to technology integration in your educational context.
Express and evaluate your beliefs about technology, teaching and learning and their influence on your own use of technology.

Compare, evaluate and apply various pedagogical and learning theories in relation to the use of educational technologies and consequential pedagogical affordances for current and emerging technologies in relation to your own pedagogical context.
Critically analyse and debate contested issues associated with existing and emergent technologies with reference to scholarly research and theories.

Design and justify a range of your own technology-enhanced learning activities with reference to your beliefs, learning theories and pedagogies, attributes of effective technology practices and potential barriers to implementation.

assessment_details.title: Assessment Task 1: Concept Map and Reflective Essay
assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment, you will create a concept map that represents your current beliefs about teaching and learning, including your philosophy and pedagogical beliefs. You may use CMap, Inspiration, or another concept/mind mapping software with which you are familiar. You will use your concept map as the basis for a reflective essay. Your essay should: explain your concept map and the linkages between concepts, giving the reader a clear sense of your teaching and learning philosophy and pedagogical beliefs evaluate how technology can support aspects of your current teaching and learning philosophy. synthesise your current thinking about the role, value, and use of technology in your teaching and learning practice describe the enablers and barriers you perceive for technology integration in your own teaching context, including any concerns and potential opportunities you identify Your reflection should also demonstrate engagement with the set readings for Module 1 and draw on these readings where appropriate. assessment_details.title: Assessment Task 2: Lesson Sequence Plan and Interactive Oral
assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment, you will create a four-lesson learning sequence to be delivered through an online learning platform such as Blackboard, Blendspace, Padlet, or another appropriate digital learning environment. The purpose of this task is to demonstrate your understanding of key pedagogical concepts and your ability to make informed decisions about digital learning design for a specific group of learners. You are not required to create the full lessons for this task. Instead, you will complete the provided lesson sequence template and use it as the basis for an interactive oral. This assessment has two components: 1. Written lesson sequence plan: approximately 1000 words, plus brief explanatory annotations using the comments feature in Word You will submit a completed lesson sequence template before your interactive oral. The template should provide a concise but clear overview of your four-lesson learning sequence, including the intended learner group, learning context, syllabus links, learning intentions, success criteria, lesson activities, and key digital tools. You should use brief annotations, using the comments feature in Word, to justify key design decisions in your plan, such as your selection of learning activities, digital tools, pedagogical strategies, and supports for your intended learner group. There is no set number of annotations required. Students should use annotations where appropriate. Annotations should be concise and should not be used to add a separate essay or extended report. Your annotations should show how your planning of sequenced learning experiences has considered: students’ diverse knowledge, experiences, characteristics, and cultures understandings of how students learn the pedagogical and technological choices made in the lesson sequence learner diversity, accessibility, engagement, and potential barriers and enablers relevant course readings and/or peer-reviewed literature, where appropriate Please take into account the particular audience you are targeting, such as a specific age group, culturally diverse students, neurodivergent learners, gifted learners, or learners with special educational needs. Your plan should clearly state the age group for which the learning sequence is intended and consider different ways of learning. 2. Interactive Oral session You will participate in a 10-minute interactive oral with the lecturer or tutor. This can be completed either in person or via video camera link. Instructions on how to book your oral presentation will be given in the Week 1 workshop. During the oral, you will explain the key ideas in your plan and respond to targeted questions about your design decisions. These questions will focus on your ability to explain, justify, and critically reflect on your learning sequence. You should be prepared to discuss points including, but not limited to, the following: the learning needs of your intended learner group your pedagogical approach your choice of online platform and digital tools how the four lessons connect as a coherent learning sequence how your design supports accessibility, engagement, and learner diversity potential barriers and enablers for implementation and how you would address them how your design is informed by course readings and relevant literature Please note no PowerPoint slides are required. You can bring in visual materials to support your explanation if applicable. These interactive oral sessions, whether completed in person or via video link, will be video recorded to ensure there is an accurate record of your performance. Recordings will be retained for 12 months on a secure UQ system in accordance with UQ assessment policy. For students completing the oral session online, you will require a working webcam, headphones, and you will be required to show the room during the oral. This assessment task is to be completed live, either in person or online via video camera link. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools during the interview will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies in preparation, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. assessment_details.title: Assessment Task 3: Learning Designs for Technology Integration Portfolio and Essay
assessment_details.task_description: In this assignment, you will develop a portfolio of two detailed learning designs for technology-enhanced activities in your own professional teaching context. This task builds on Task 2. You are required to select two lessons from the four-lesson sequence plan you created in Task 2 and develop these lessons in greater detail. Your two detailed learning designs should demonstrate how technology can be used to support meaningful learning in your selected teaching context. You should clearly identify the intended learners, curriculum learning objectives, learning activities, resources required, technologies used, and strategies for supporting learner engagement and participation. Final submission You will submit a 2000 to 2500-word essay, excluding references and appendices. Your two detailed learning designs should be included in the appendices. Your essay should provide a rationale for the designs. In particular, your essay should: explain how your two detailed learning designs align with the relevant curriculum learning objectives justify how learning will occur through the two learning designs identify and evaluate the instructional design features of your technology-enhanced activities using relevant models and literature justify your designs in relation to current learning theories and pedagogies articulate your beliefs about technology, teaching, and learning, and explain how these beliefs underpin your designs address potential barriers to the implementation of your designs outline an evaluation strategy for your designs demonstrate breadth of knowledge of literature relating to learning and instructional design theories Your two detailed learning designs should be included as appendices and should provide enough practical detail for the reader to understand how the lessons would be implemented.
